icd10_codes.description: Migraine with aura, not intractable, without status migrainosus

dialogue:
[doctor] hi , {PATIENT_FIRST} . i'm doctor {DOCTOR_LAST} . have a seat . what brings you in today ?
[patient] hey doctor {DOCTOR_LAST} . honestly i'm not sure what's going on . my left hand keeps going numb and tingly , like it fell asleep , and it's happened about four times this month .
[doctor] okay . when did it first start ?
[patient] i think the first one was around {DATE_SPOKEN} . i was at work , i drive a forklift on the night shift at the warehouse , and my hand just went dead on the controls .
[doctor] that sounds scary when you're running heavy equipment . what did you do ?
[patient] i pulled over , shook it out , and it came back after maybe ten minutes . i kept working because we were short staffed , which i know was dumb .
[doctor] it's understandable . tell me about the episodes . do they come with anything else ? headache , vision changes , trouble talking ?
[patient] the headaches , yeah . i've been getting them since i was a teenager . it's one side of my head , throbbing , and i need to lie down in a dark room . but the numbness is new .
[doctor] okay . before the numbness started , did you get any warning ? like zigzag lights or blind spots ?
[patient] yes , actually . i see these wavy lines in the left side of my vision for about twenty minutes , then the hand goes numb , then the headache comes .
[doctor] that pattern is important . the wavy lines before the headache sound like an aura . how often are the headaches ?
[patient] maybe two or three times a month . i take ibuprofen and sometimes i take sumatriptan . i picked the sumatriptan up at the pharmacy a while back .
[doctor] how often are you taking the sumatriptan ?
[patient] like twice a month when it's bad .
[doctor] okay . any weakness in your face or your arm when the numbness happens ? is your speech ever slurred ?
[patient] no , my speech is fine . my hand is just tingly and dead feeling . i can still grip stuff but it's weak .
[doctor] when did the headaches first start ?
[patient] {YEAR} , i think . i got my first ever migraine diagnosis that summer after a bad week at work .
[doctor] okay . any family history of strokes or migraines ?
[patient] my grandmother had a stroke when she was about seventy . my mom gets migraines too .
[doctor] okay . and what about smoking , alcohol , any drugs ?
[patient] i quit smoking last year . i have maybe two beers on weekends . nothing else .
[doctor] good . how's your sleep on night shift ?
[patient] terrible . i sleep in the morning with blackout curtains and i get maybe five hours . i think that's part of it .
[doctor] that could definitely contribute . how about caffeine ?
[patient] i drink like four energy drinks on shift . i know .
[doctor] okay . let me do a quick neuro exam . can you follow my finger with your eyes ?
[patient] yes .
[doctor] squeeze my hands . push against me . strength looks normal on both sides . touch here , tell me where you feel it .
[patient] the left hand feels duller . the fingers especially .
[doctor] okay . your reflexes look symmetric . gait is normal . blood pressure is one twenty six over seventy eight , pulse seventy two .
[patient] that's good .
[doctor] i'd like to get an mri of your brain with contrast to be safe , plus blood work and an ecg , since you're young but you're having new sensory symptoms .
[patient] okay . will i need to stop driving the forklift ?
[doctor] for now i'd hold off on operating heavy equipment until we know what's causing the numbness . i'll write you a note for your supervisor .
[patient] my supervisor is going to be so annoyed . i'm already on the schedule through the holidays . and i can't afford to miss shifts as a forklift operator .
[doctor] i understand . that's why i want to get this done quickly . can you come in for the mri this week ?
[patient] yeah , i can do thursday morning . my last physical was on {DATE_NUM} and everything was fine .
[doctor] great . for the headaches , keep a headache diary with dates and triggers . i don't want you taking sumatriptan more than two days a week because overusing it can cause rebound headaches .
[patient] okay . so no more ibuprofen every day either ?
[doctor] right , limit the ibuprofen too . do you have any questions ?
[patient] no , not really . i'm just worried it's something serious like a stroke .
[doctor] at your age that's unlikely , but the mri will tell us . if you get weakness in your face or your arm that doesn't go away , slurred speech , or the worst headache of your life , call 911 right away .
[patient] got it . thank you , doctor {DOCTOR_LAST} .
[doctor] you're welcome . we'll see you thursday .
note:
CHIEF COMPLAINT

Intermittent left hand numbness and recurrent headaches.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

{PATIENT_FIRST} {PATIENT_LAST} is a {AGE}-year-old male with a long-standing history of migraine who presents with about four episodes of left hand numbness over the past month. He works as a forklift operator on the night shift at the warehouse. The first episode occurred around {DATE_SPOKEN} while he was operating equipment; he pulled over and symptoms resolved in about ten minutes. He continued working that night.

Migraine diagnosis was made in {YEAR}. Each episode is preceded by approximately twenty minutes of visual aura described as wavy lines in the left visual field, followed by numbness of the left fingers and then a unilateral throbbing headache lasting several hours. He denies facial droop, dysarthria, or focal weakness of the leg. He takes sumatriptan roughly twice a month and ibuprofen intermittently. He reports five hours of sleep on his night shift schedule and drinks approximately four energy drinks per shift. He quit smoking last year and drinks two beers on weekends.

Family history is notable for a grandmother with stroke in her seventies and a mother with migraine. His last physical was on {DATE_NUM}.

PHYSICAL EXAM

BP 126/78, pulse 72. Neurological examination shows full extraocular movements, symmetric strength, and intact speech. Sensation to light touch is mildly decreased in the left fingers. Reflexes are symmetric and gait is normal.

RESULTS

MRI brain with contrast scheduled. Basic labs and ECG ordered.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

1. Migraine with aura with transient left hand paresthesia. Differential includes migraine aura versus transient ischemic event given family history, though the age and aura pattern favor migraine. Imaging was selected in line with the Washington guidelines for new-onset headache with focal symptoms. MRI brain with and without contrast, ECG, and basic labs ordered. Advised to hold operation of heavy equipment until workup is complete; work note provided.

2. Recurrent headache with frequent acute medication use. Limit sumatriptan to no more than two days per week and ibuprofen to avoid medication overuse headache. Start headache diary tracking dates and triggers.

3. Sleep disruption and caffeine use on night shift. Counseled on sleep hygiene and reducing energy drink intake.

Return precautions reviewed, including persistent arm weakness, slurred speech, or a sudden worst headache, with instruction to call 911.
